messages:
cheng: Heads-up: seeing a spike of 503s from kube-apiserver in eu-west-1 starting ~09:12 UTC. Controller-manager shows reconcilers stuck when new GPU nodes attach.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-4729. Pager duty alerted.
samir: Can you paste the apiserver logs? 503s + controller-manager stalls sounds like either fd exhaustion or proxy SNAT exhaustion.
cheng: Putting logs: 
```
Apr  9 09:12:45 node kube-apiserver[1234]: apiserver: response error 503: dial tcp 10.4.2.15:2379: connect: no route to host
Apr  9 09:12:46 node kube-apiserver[1234]: WARNING: accept EMFILE: too many open files
Apr  9 09:12:47 node kube-controller-manager[2345]: reconcile failed: timeout waiting for watch stream
```
jess: Noticed onboarding flow for dedicated GPU pool did a simultaneous 120-node attach in eu-west-1 at 09:11. That matches timeframe. Those nodes hit the apiserver watch fanout.
alex: If it's EMFILE then ulimits first. Check `cat /proc/$(pidof kube-apiserver)/limits | grep open` and `lsof -p $(pidof kube-apiserver) | wc -l`. Also check kube-proxy SNAT table usage on the NAT instances.
maria: NAT SNAT free ports are low in eu-west-1 public subnet. We had a burst earlier for model-serving canaries. SNAT logs show port exhaustion at 09:12:20.
samir: Confirmed: `conntrack -S` shows high entries; `kubectl get pods -A -o wide` shows many model-serving pods in Pending -> Running loop. Probably clients re-trying to apiserver as they get stuck, amplifying connections.
cheng: Quick mitigation: reduced onboarding concurrency in the autoscaler (set maxParallel=10) and rolled a kube-proxy config to enable endpointLocalTrafficPolicy. Also bump apiserver --max-requests-inflight from 400 to 800 temporarily.
jess: We also flipped a circuit to route non-critical control traffic to a read-replica apiserver pool to reduce primary fanout. :white_check_mark:
alex: Long-term: consider prefix/KV caching on the serving side for join events and gate onboarding with a staged handshake to avoid watch storms. Also file to increase apiserver FD soft limit in systemd unit and validate against worst-case attach surge.
maria: I'll open a ticket to request larger NATs or move GPU onboarding into a VPC with larger SNAT capacity for eu-west.
samir: Action items: 1) increase apiserver ulimit (cheng) 2) provision additional NAT capacity (maria) 3) add onboarding concurrency guard to autoscaler (jess) 4) run controlled load test for 150-node attach (alex).
cheng: Acked, running the apiserver systemd change now and will monitor. Posting quick check commands:
```
# fd count
lsof -p $(pidof kube-apiserver) | wc -l
# conntrack
conntrack -S
# nat table
sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v | grep SNAT
```
oncall-bot: Update: mitigation applied (apiserver ulimit bump, autoscaler concurrency reduced). Monitoring alerts suppressed for 30m.
samir: We'll keep the incident open until 24h without recurrence. For the notes: probably label this as "watch-fanout + SNAT port exhaustion during GPU onboarding" in postmortem.
cheng: Thanks everyone, will follow up with a short postmortem draft in #postmortems once we have metrics. :thumbsup:
